q-135366.name: Question 1
q-135366.problem:
Find the inverse of the following matrix:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
q-135366.worked_solution:
The given matrix can be obtained from the identity matrix by permuting its columns. Therefore, $A$ is a permutation matrix.

The inverse of a permutation matrix can be found as follows: 

$$
{P}^{-1}={P}^{T}
$$

In our case, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1}={[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{-1}={[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
q-135375.worked_solution:
The given matrix can be obtained from the identity matrix by permuting its columns. Therefore, $A$ is a permutation matrix.

The inverse of a permutation matrix can be found as follows: 

$$
{P}^{-1}={P}^{T}
$$

In our case, we obtain

$$

q-135390.name: Question 3
q-135390.problem:
Find the inverse of the following matrix:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
q-135390.worked_solution:
Notice that we're given a Frobenius matrix:

- all entries on the main diagonal are ones

- the matrix has only one column (the $1$st column) where some entries below the main diagonal are not zeros

- all the other entries outside the main diagonal are zeros

To find the inverse of a Frobenius matrix, we simply take the non-zero entries outside the main diagonal with opposite signs. 

In our case, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1}={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Find the inverse of the following matrix:

A=[1000−11004010−2001]

a
[1−14−2010000100001]
b
[10001100−40102001]
c
[1000110014010−12001]
d
[10001100−1401012001]
e
[11−42010000100001]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Notice that we're given a Frobenius matrix:

  • all entries on the main diagonal are ones

  • the matrix has only one column (the 1st column) where some entries below the main diagonal are not zeros

  • all the other entries outside the main diagonal are zeros

To find the inverse of a Frobenius matrix, we simply take the non-zero entries outside the main diagonal with opposite signs.

In our case, we obtain

A−1=[1000−11004010−2001]−1=[10001100−40102001].

q-135391.problem:
Find the inverse of the following matrix:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{5} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
q-135391.worked_solution:
Notice that we're given a Frobenius matrix:

- all entries on the main diagonal are ones

- the matrix has only one column (the $2$nd column) where some entries below the main diagonal are not zeros

- all the other entries outside the main diagonal are zeros

To find the inverse of a Frobenius matrix, we simply take the non-zero entries outside the main diagonal with opposite signs. 

In our case, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1}={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{5} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{5} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Find the inverse of the following matrix:

A=[10000100015100−301]

a
[1000010005100−1301]
b
[100001000−15100301]
c
[100001−15300100001]
d
[100001000−51001301]
e
[1000015−1300100001]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Notice that we're given a Frobenius matrix:

  • all entries on the main diagonal are ones

  • the matrix has only one column (the 2nd column) where some entries below the main diagonal are not zeros

  • all the other entries outside the main diagonal are zeros

To find the inverse of a Frobenius matrix, we simply take the non-zero entries outside the main diagonal with opposite signs.

In our case, we obtain

A−1=[10000100015100−301]−1=[100001000−15100301].

q-135398.problem:
Find the inverse of the following matrix:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{4} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -8 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
q-135398.worked_solution:
Notice that we're given a Frobenius matrix:

- all entries on the main diagonal are ones

- the matrix has only one column (the $2$nd column) where some entries below the main diagonal are not zeros

- all the other entries outside the main diagonal are zeros

To find the inverse of a Frobenius matrix, we simply take the non-zero entries outside the main diagonal with opposite signs. 

In our case, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1}={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{4} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -8 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{4} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Find the inverse of the following matrix:

A=[10000100014100−801]

a
[100001000−14100801]
b
[100001000−41001801]
c
[100001−14800100001]
d
[100001−41800100001]
e
[1000010004100−1801]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Notice that we're given a Frobenius matrix:

  • all entries on the main diagonal are ones

To find the inverse of a Frobenius matrix, we simply take the non-zero entries outside the main diagonal with opposite signs.
